businesses.existingSiteNote: Has an old 2016 HTTP-only template site (deaconshousecafe.co.uk) that Google Maps does NOT link. Effectively invisible to customers. This makes the modern-site pitch even stronger.
businesses.story: A cafe inside the 17th-century close where Deacon William Brodie lived his double life — respected councilor by day, head of a burglary gang by night. Hanged 1788. Robert Louis Stevenson used him as the seed for Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde. The cafe serves smoked Ayrshire bacon, free-range eggs, home-made scones with Craigie's Farm jam, organic Fairtrade coffee.

design.palette: Edinburgh slate-grey + Scottish heather purple + whisky amber + parchment + flame orange (rooted in Brodie's Close stone, heather moors, Scotch whisky)
design.layout: Dual-identity scroll grammar — day cafe up top (light parchment), night history at bottom (dark slate), bridged by Stevenson quote divider. Scroll triggers day-to-night palette transition.
design.motion: Two signature motions: (1) fixed gaslamp SVG with irregular candle-flicker animation top-right; (2) vertical tartan-rule down left edge that fills with woven tartan pattern proportional to scroll position. Neither exists on any other site in the radar.

emailDraft.subject: Your cafe in Brodie's Close — a quiet idea for the front of house
emailDraft.body:
Hello,

I walked through Brodie's Close last week and stopped at Deacon's House Cafe. The smoked salmon on the artisan farmhouse bread was excellent, and the cream tea was the most honest one I've had in Edinburgh in a long while.

I noticed Google Maps doesn't link a website for you — and the older site at deaconshousecafe.co.uk isn't connected from there, so most people walking past on the Royal Mile never find it. I make small, beautiful sites for cafes like yours and I built two previews for Deacon's, free, to show what's possible.

The quiet editorial one (perfect for a Royal Mile cafe):
https://giladmeishar.github.io/cowork-radar/deacon-house-cafe-edinburgh-20260525-basic.html

And the one I really wanted to make — built around the 1788 story, with the day cafe up top and the Brodie history at the bottom, the way the close itself feels:
https://giladmeishar.github.io/cowork-radar/deacon-house-cafe-edinburgh-20260525-premium.html

The domain deaconshousecafe.com is available at around £12/year. If you ever wanted to use either of these, or wanted me to adjust them, just reply and I'll make any change you ask for. Otherwise, please ignore — I won't email a second time.

With warm regards from a guest who enjoyed your scones.

—
This is a one-time message. If you'd rather I didn't email again, just reply with 'no thanks' and I will note it down.
emailDraft.bodyHebrew: הקדמתי, שכתבתי לבעל הקפה Deacon's House Cafe באדינבורו — מקום ב-Brodie's Close ברויאל מייל, בלי אתר מקושר מ-Google Maps. הסברתי שהאתר הישן שלהם מ-2016 לא מקושר מ-Maps, אז לקוחות פוטנציאליים לא מוצאים אותו. צירפתי שתי תצוגות מקדימות חינמיות — בסיסית עריכתית + פרמיום שבנוי סביב הסיפור של דיקון בריאודי משנת 1788. הזכרתי שדומיין .com של העסק זמין ב-~£12 לשנה. סיימתי בהבטחה שזה מסר חד-פעמי.

businesses.name: Konoba Zbondini

businesses.emailSource: WebSearch + matches business naming convention (konoba.businessname@gmail.com pattern of small Croatian businesses)
businesses.story: Family konoba in Velo Grablje — once a lavender-capital village on Hvar, now near-empty. Famous for peka (lamb/octopus under an iron bell with embers), gregada (Dalmatian fishermen's stew), home olive oil, plavac mali wine. By reservation only in summer evenings.

design.palette: Adriatic blue + Croatian lavender purple + sun-bleached limestone + terracotta + olive green — rooted in Hvar's stone-village identity
design.layout: Full-bleed Ken-Burns hero with overlapping serif, narrative village-story sticky column, signature 'peka' moment with concentric circle motif, 3-column staggered dish cards, Adriatic deep-blue visit section
design.motion: Lavender stem SVG sways in top-right corner, hero photo slow zoom, ribbon marquee of menu ingredients, scroll-driven palette shift from limestone-warm to Adriatic-deep

emailDraft.subject: A small idea for Zbondini — built with love from a guest
emailDraft.body:
Pozdrav,

I visited Velo Grablje this season — the konoba was already full and the peka smell led us up from Brusje. The gregada was the best I've had.

I noticed there's no website where guests can read about you or book the peka ahead. I make small, beautiful sites for places like Zbondini, and I built two free previews:

Classical:
https://giladmeishar.github.io/cowork-radar/konoba-zbondini-velo-grablje-20260526-basic.html

The one I really wanted to make — Adriatic-blue, lavender, the peka as the centerpiece:
https://giladmeishar.github.io/cowork-radar/konoba-zbondini-velo-grablje-20260526-premium.html

A domain like konobazbondini.com runs about €12/year. If you ever want to use either, or want me to adjust them, just reply. Otherwise please ignore — this is a one-time message.

Hvala i pozdrav iz lavandinog sela.

—
This is a one-time message.
